data.narrative:
Cellino is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Nabiha Saklayen and Marinna Madrid that has raised approximately $125M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparables universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies in the Biotech & Health sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, Chai Discovery, New Limit, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

The peer-median method is inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparable data. Of the 8 same-sector private peers identified, fewer than 3 companies satisfy simultaneous filters for stage, timing, and valuation tier—the minimum threshold for reliable median construction. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because Cellino's revenue is not on file, which is typical for private biotech companies at this stage. The sector median P/S multiple for the 3 public comparables stands at 5.63x, but without disclosed revenue, this multiple offers no direct valuation input.

The lack of applicable quantitative methods reflects constraints inherent to early-stage biotech valuation: private companies in this sector rarely disclose revenue, and true peer sets at the Series A stage remain thin. A credible valuation range would require either (1) access to Cellino's revenue or ARR figures, (2) identification of additional same-stage private comps with disclosed metrics, or (3) reliance on alternative frameworks such as DCF or venture capital method calibrated to company-specific development milestones and capital efficiency. Current data is insufficient to triangulate a supported valuation range.
